input.quote: (a) Assignment. Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
input.rationale: Section 10.2(a) imposes a symmetric consent requirement on our Depositor and on Cellco as Servicer, but expressly carves out Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 lets the Depositor's merger/consolidation counterparty, business successor, or an Affiliate assignee become the successor Depositor without consent (notice/officer's certificate and opinions only), which is the affiliate/successor M&A carve-out the playbook requires; Section 7.6 gives Cellco the mirror-image treatment. The Issuer is not restricted at all, and Section 2.2 acknowledges the Issuer's assignment and pledge of the Depositor Transferred Property to the Indenture Trustee for the Secured Parties, so our financing-side transfers are preserved and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. There is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the document (no "change of control" language), and Section 7.1 is a "No Resignation" covenant barring Cellco from resigning unless legally unable to perform, so the counterparty has no exit or re-pricing right on our reorganisation — the walk-away scenarios are absent. Two points short of the pure preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the third-party consent gate is not expressed as "not to be unreasonably withheld" and there is no competitor bar on a Servicer assignment (both are structural noteholder/rating-agency protections in a securitization and apply symmetrically), and Section 6.4 permits Cellco free delegation while it is Servicer or Custodian — acceptable because no delegation or contracting relieves it of responsibility for those obligations. On its material terms the package sits at or above the fallback (mutual assignment to successors with notice), so we do not redline.
